chapter: Early life and training in Boston
title: First piano lessons, boy soprano choir and boyhood jobs
summary: His mother gives him piano lessons, a candy-eating first teacher is replaced by a German, he sings in the Malden boys' choir, and he names his siblings and school-age jobs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But before that my mother gave me music lessons and she give me a teacher and the teacher used to sit there and eat candy and I'd make a whole lot of mistakes and I told my mother about it so we got another -- we got a German.
Where was this in Boston or Fairfax.

This was in Everett, Massachusetts and he used to give me piano lessons and I would go out to the Malden, to the church there and sing in this choir. We had a boy's choir out there and I had a high voice. I could sing E above the scale, and I was one of his leading boy sopranos and for quite awhile I used to walk about two or three miles to the church and have rehearsals and one winter I got my feet
wet and that was the end of my singing. That was in Malden, Massachusetts.
I forgot to ask you, did you have an brothers or sisters.

Yeah, I had two sisters and a brother. I had another brother but he died. I think that's -- my sister's name was -- one was Edna, she was the oldest. Viola was the next and then my brother he came next and he's the one that died and then there's me and then my brother Rudolph. He was the youngest.
You had two brothers, then. And two sisters.

Yeah. And we got along pretty good, and while I was in Everett I went to school there and during the school, during that term I used to take care of the doctor's horse and then I had a paper route, you know, sell papers go around there and then in the summertime I'd go in the factory, shoe factory and cut uppers. Oh, I was very industrious. Anyway I kept my music up and I remember when I was in the eighth grade, I played Beethoven's Opus 49 and my mother said why did you duck-bow and I said oh, them kids, they know. I didn't have to bow for them.
